materials.name: Hawk Flight Feathers
materials.desc: Stiff, barred primaries that cut the air with a faint hiss. Fletchers swear arrows fledged with them fly truer.

materials.name: Hawk Eye
materials.desc: A tiny amber orb with a pinprick pupil that seems to track movement even after death. Ground into far-seeing tinctures.

materials.name: Hunter Shark Tooth
materials.desc: A serrated, triangular fang the size of a thumb, endlessly replaced in life. Set into clubs, necklaces and saw-blades.

materials.name: Hunter Shark Skin
materials.desc: Grey hide covered in tiny tooth-like scales that rasp one way and slide the other. Used for grips and as a woodworker's file.

materials.name: Hunter Shark Liver Oil
materials.desc: A pungent golden oil rendered from the enormous liver. Divers rub it on to keep out the chill and sharpen their sense of the water.

materials.name: Hunter Shark Scent Pits
materials.desc: Paired pitted sacs from the snout that can taste one drop of blood in a bay. Alchemists prize them for tracking draughts.

materials.name: Shark Meat
materials.desc: Dense pale flesh with a sharp ammonia tang unless soaked in brine. Filling fare on long voyages.

materials.name: Hyena Hide
materials.desc: Coarse, spotted fur with a rank carrion smell that never quite leaves. Cheap cloaks and tent flaps.

materials.name: Hyena Jawbone
materials.desc: A heavy, blunt-toothed jaw built to crush marrow bones. Talismans of it are said to bolster a warrior among allies.

materials.name: Hyena Cackle Gland
materials.desc: A slick throat gland that swells when the beast cackles. Tricksters distil it into draughts that provoke helpless laughter.

materials.name: Jackal Pelt
materials.desc: A thin, sandy pelt with black-tipped guard hairs. Blends well into dunes and dry scrub.

materials.name: Jackal Ears
materials.desc: Tall, thin ears with velvet backs. Dried and powdered, they go into potions for keen hearing.

materials.name: Killer Whale Blubber
materials.desc: Thick slabs of white fat that render into clear lamp oil and cold-proof salves.

materials.name: Killer Whale Tooth
materials.desc: A conical ivory tooth, dense and creamy, scrimshawed by sailors into charms of the hunt.

materials.name: Killer Whale Echo Melon
materials.desc: The waxy lens of fat in the forehead with which it 'sees' by sound. Alchemists use it for blindsight and echo-tracking elixirs.

materials.name: Killer Whale Hide
materials.desc: Glossy black-and-white skin, rubbery and waterproof. Makes excellent boat covers and wet-weather boots.

materials.name: Killer Whale Lungs
materials.desc: Huge, spongy lungs that hold breath for a quarter hour. Key reagent in water-breathing and deep-diving potions.

materials.name: Lion Mane
materials.desc: A heavy ruff of tawny-to-black hair. Worn by champions, it lends a roaring presence that unsettles foes.

materials.name: Lion Pelt
materials.desc: Short golden fur over a supple hide. Warm enough for nights on the savanna.

materials.name: Lion Heart
materials.desc: A big, powerful heart that some warriors eat raw before battle. Alchemists steep it into draughts against fright.

materials.name: Lion Claw
materials.desc: A thick, hooked claw sheathed in a horny cap. Popular in ceremonial gauntlets and hunt-trophies.

materials.name: Lizard Tail
materials.desc: A still-twitching tail that grows back on its owner. Hedge-healers grind it into salves for knitting flesh.

materials.name: Mammoth Ivory
materials.desc: A great spiralling tusk of cream-and-brown ivory, heavy as a log. Carvers make hafts, shields and runes that never crack in frost.

materials.name: Mammoth Wool
materials.desc: Long, oily red-brown hair over a dense underfleece. Woven, it keeps out even killing cold.

materials.name: Mammoth Hide
materials.desc: An inch-thick hide tough as boiled leather even raw. Makes heavy hide armour and yurt walls.

materials.name: Mammoth Fat
materials.desc: Firm yellow tallow from the hump. Burns long, and as a salve keeps frostbite at bay.

materials.name: Mammoth Meat
materials.desc: Dark, rich meat marbled with fat. One beast feeds a village for a moon if salted.

materials.name: Mastiff Hide
materials.desc: Short-haired, thick-skinned dog hide. Used for straps and cheap jerkins.

materials.name: Mastiff Nose
materials.desc: The damp black nose and scent membranes, dried and ground for tracking potions.

materials.name: Mule Hide
materials.desc: Tough, dun-coloured hide that tans into hard-wearing leather for packs.

materials.name: Mule Sinew
materials.desc: Long back tendons that never seem to tire. Braided into straps for bags that carry more than they should.

materials.name: Mule Hoof
materials.desc: A small, hard hoof, sure on scree. Rendered into glue or carved into charms for sure-footedness.

materials.name: Octopus Ink Sac
materials.desc: A small sac of inky black fluid that billows into a cloud in water. Makes a fine ink and smoke-concealing reagents.

materials.name: Octopus Chromatic Skin
materials.desc: Soft, slippery skin speckled with colour cells that still shimmer when stroked. Used in camouflage dyes.

materials.name: Octopus Tentacle
materials.desc: A sucker-lined arm; chewy grilled, and the suckers are dried for grip-enhancing glue.

materials.name: Owl Feather
materials.desc: A soft, fringed feather that makes no sound when brushed. Sewn into cloaks and boots for silent movement.

materials.name: Owl Eye
materials.desc: A huge, tubular golden eye that reflects the faintest light. Base of night-sight tinctures.

materials.name: Panther Pelt
materials.desc: A sleek black pelt with faint ghost-rosettes visible in sidelight. Drinks torchlight; beloved of thieves.

materials.name: Panther Claw
materials.desc: A needle-sharp, retractable claw. Set in climbing gloves and pounce-charms.

materials.name: Panther Hamstring
materials.desc: Springy leg tendons that power the leap. Used as bowstrings and in agility draughts.

materials.name: Plesiosaurus Flipper
materials.desc: A broad, leathery paddle over a lattice of finger-bones. Crafted into fins and swimming gear.

materials.name: Plesiosaurus Lung
materials.desc: An elastic, oversized lung that holds air for long dives. Rendered into breath-holding elixirs.

materials.name: Plesiosaurus Neck Vertebrae
materials.desc: A string of disc-shaped bones from the long neck. Carved into flexible whips, flutes and beads.

materials.name: Plesiosaurus Hide
materials.desc: Smooth, greenish reptile skin that sheds water easily.

materials.name: Poisonous Snake Venom
materials.desc: A few drops of clear, amber-tinged venom. The standard base of cheap blade poisons and antivenom.

materials.name: Snakeskin
materials.desc: Thin patterned skin, supple as silk. Used for belts, scabbard wraps and purses.

materials.name: Snake Fang
materials.desc: A hollow, needle-thin fang. Tinkerers use them as poison-injection needles.

materials.name: Polar Bear Pelt
materials.desc: Dense white fur over black skin, invisible against snow. Makes the warmest cloaks in the north.

materials.name: Polar Bear Fat
materials.desc: Thick, clean-smelling fat. Rubbed into skin or brewed with herbs, it wards off killing cold.

materials.name: Polar Bear Claw
materials.desc: A dark, curved claw made for gripping ice. Set in ice-picks and crampons.

materials.name: Polar Bear Liver
materials.desc: A dark, dense liver so rich it sickens anyone who eats it. Poisoners render it into a slow wasting toxin.

materials.name: Bear Meat
materials.desc: Strong-tasting red meat; must be cooked through.

materials.name: Horsehide
materials.desc: Dense, even-grained hide that tans into fine leather for saddles and shoes.

materials.name: Quipper Teeth
materials.desc: Tiny razor-edged teeth that interlock like a saw. Set in rows along weapon edges to make them rend.

materials.name: Quipper Scales
materials.desc: Silver-red scales that flash in the light. Used as sequins and in fishing lures.

materials.name: Rat Tail
materials.desc: A scaly, naked tail. Hedge-witches knot them into charms against — or for — sickness.

materials.name: Rat Incisors
materials.desc: Orange, chisel-like front teeth that never stop growing. Ground into gnaw-powder that weakens rope and wood.

materials.name: Raven Feather
materials.desc: A glossy black feather with a purple-green sheen. Scribes cut quills from it for memory-inks and message scrolls.

materials.name: Raven Tongue
materials.desc: A small, surprisingly human-like tongue. Dried and powdered for mimicry and voice-throwing charms.

materials.name: Reef Shark Tooth
materials.desc: A small, sharp triangular tooth. Strung into necklaces and set in coral weapons.

materials.name: Reef Shark Skin
materials.desc: Rough, sandpapery grey skin used as a grip wrap and polishing file.

materials.name: Reef Shark Oil
materials.desc: A thin yellow oil from the liver; divers smear it on to slip through water.

materials.name: Rhinoceros Horn
materials.desc: A dense, fibrous horn, heavy as stone. Carved into ram-heads for shields and prized in potions of might.

materials.name: Rhinoceros Hide
materials.desc: Plated grey hide nearly two fingers thick. Tanned into shields and hide armour that turns blades.

materials.name: Rhinoceros Meat
materials.desc: Lean, coarse red meat, best stewed.

materials.name: Horse Meat
materials.desc: Sweet, dark red meat; taboo in many lands, a staple in others.

materials.name: Riding Horse Sinew
materials.desc: Long leg tendons that dry into cord-like strands. Used in horseshoes-of-speed charms and bowstrings.

materials.name: Warhorse Heart
materials.desc: A great, dense heart that kept the beast charging into spears. Alchemists steep it in draughts of endurance.

materials.name: Warhorse Hoof
materials.desc: A dinner-plate hoof, hard as stone. Carved into luck charms and ground as a binder for speed potions.

materials.name: Saber-Toothed Tiger Fang
materials.desc: A curved, flattened tusk as long as a dagger with a serrated back edge. Hafted as a knife or set in ceremonial helms.

materials.name: Saber-Toothed Tiger Pelt
materials.desc: A dense, pale-striped pelt made for snow-shadow ambushes. Warm and hard to spot in winter woods.

materials.name: Saber-Toothed Tiger Claw
materials.desc: A heavy, hooked claw built to pin prey. Trophy and gauntlet material.

materials.name: Scorpion Stinger
materials.desc: A curved amber barb with a bulb of venom behind it. Poisoners milk it for painful toxins.

materials.name: Scorpion Carapace
materials.desc: A hard, translucent shell that glows faintly under moonlight. Used in lacquer and inlay.

materials.name: Dried Sea Horse
materials.desc: A curled, bony little body dried stiff. Carried as a charm or ground into water-breathing tonics.

materials.name: Spider Silk
materials.desc: A fine, sticky thread spooled from the spinnerets. Weavers blend it into strong, near-invisible cord.

materials.name: Spider Venom
materials.desc: A pinhead of potent venom. Used in weak sleep- and pain-poisons.

materials.name: Tiger Pelt
materials.desc: Rich orange fur banded with black, perfect camouflage among reeds. A prestige cloak and hunter's mantle.

materials.name: Tiger Whiskers
materials.desc: Stiff, white whiskers that feel the air in pitch darkness. Tied into charms for moving silently at night.

materials.name: Tiger Fang
materials.desc: A long, ivory canine. Worn as a sign of valour or set in a hunter's knife pommel.

materials.name: Tiger Sinew
materials.desc: Powerful haunch tendons that drive the pounce. Used for bowstrings and agility tonics.

materials.name: Triceratops Frill
materials.desc: A broad, shield-shaped plate of bone fringed with knobs. Split and dressed, it makes a natural shield that shrugs off blows.

materials.name: Triceratops Horn
materials.desc: A metre-long brow horn, dense and sharp. Hafted as a lance-head or ram and used in potions of the charge.

materials.name: Triceratops Nose Horn
materials.desc: A short, blunt nasal horn; good material for axe-heads and hammers.

materials.name: Triceratops Hide
materials.desc: Pebbly, thick hide that tans into sturdy armour.

materials.name: Triceratops Meat
materials.desc: Heavy, beefy meat; one beast feeds a war-band for weeks.

materials.name: Tyrannosaurus Rex Tooth
materials.desc: A banana-sized, serrated fang that can punch through plate. Warlords wear them to inspire terror; smiths set them as sword-points.

materials.name: Tyrannosaurus Rex Heart
materials.desc: A barrel-sized heart that still quivers an hour after death. Brewed into draughts of monstrous strength and fearlessness.

materials.name: Tyrannosaurus Rex Voice Box
materials.desc: A cavernous throat resonator that shaped the killing roar. Horn-makers build terrifying war-horns around it.

materials.name: Tyrannosaurus Rex Hide
materials.desc: Heavy, scaled hide mottled green and brown. Tans into imposing and very tough hide armour.

materials.name: Tyrannosaurus Rex Meat
materials.desc: Tough, gamey meat. Warriors of some jungle tribes eat it for courage.

materials.name: Vulture Feather
materials.desc: A dusty brown pinion that smells faintly of the dead. Used by morticians and in funeral fans.

materials.name: Vulture Gizzard
materials.desc: A tough, acid-soaked stomach that digests rot without sickening. The base of cheap anti-disease remedies.

materials.name: Weasel Pelt
materials.desc: A slim, glossy pelt that turns white in winter. Trim for hoods and a traditional charm of slipping out of trouble.

materials.name: Wolf Pelt
materials.desc: Thick grey fur with a dense winter underlayer. The classic ranger's cloak and bedroll.

materials.name: Wolf Fang
materials.desc: A long, hooked canine. Worn on cords by trackers, said to keep the pack's instincts sharp.

materials.name: Wolf Nose
materials.desc: The scent-gland lined snout. Dried and powdered for tracking tinctures.

materials.name: Bat Wing Membranes (bundle)
materials.desc: A handful of thin, leathery wing-webs. Cured and powdered, they go into flying and echo-sense draughts.

materials.name: Bat Guano
materials.desc: Dry, crumbly droppings rich in saltpetre. Farmers and firework-makers both want it.

materials.name: Bat Ears (bundle)
materials.desc: Dozens of tiny, ribbed ears. Ground, they grant keen hearing and a sense for echoes.

materials.name: Beetle Carapace Chips
materials.desc: Iridescent green-and-bronze shell chips. Glued in overlapping rows they make lacquered armour inlays.

materials.name: Beetle Dye Paste
materials.desc: Crushed beetles yield a deep crimson paste. Dyers and scribes prize it.

materials.name: Centipede Venom Claws
materials.desc: Paired pincer-fangs full of numbing venom. Ground into numbing salves or mild paralytic poisons.

materials.name: Centipede Segments
materials.desc: Hard, red-brown body segments. Strung into rattles and climbing-charms.

materials.name: Insect Chitin Dust
materials.desc: A glittering, crunchy dust of crushed wings and shells. A cheap binder for alchemical pastes.

materials.name: Insect Wings (bundle)
materials.desc: A pouch of gauzy, rainbow-sheened wings that hum when blown across. Used in flight and buzzing-noise charms.

materials.name: Quipper Meat
materials.desc: Bony little fillets, sweet if fried crisp.

materials.name: Raven Eye
materials.desc: A bead-black glittering eye. Scryers grind it into inks that remember what was written.

materials.name: Wasp Stingers
materials.desc: A pouch of tiny, barbed stingers still loaded with venom. Makes a stinging, swelling poison.

materials.name: Wasp Paper Nest
materials.desc: A grey, layered paper comb chewed from wood pulp. Burns hot and fast; makes excellent tinder and light paper.

materials.name: Wasp Larvae
materials.desc: Plump white grubs from the comb. Toasted, a crunchy delicacy in some lands.

materials.name: Hawk Talon
materials.desc: A black, needle-hooked talon that closes like a trap. Falconers' charms and arrowhead barbs.

materials.name: Owl Talon
materials.desc: A pale, feather-sheathed talon. Night-hunters wear them as charms for a silent strike.

materials.name: Hunter Shark Jaw
materials.desc: The whole cartilage jaw, bristling with teeth, dried into a gaping trophy. Mounted over tavern doors or built into war-helms.

materials.name: Octopus Beak
materials.desc: A small, parrot-like black beak, hard as horn. Carved into fishhooks and clever-charm pendants.

materials.name: Tiger Bone
materials.desc: Heavy, dense leg bones. Steeped in strong spirits for liniments said to lend a tiger's vigour.

materials.name: Mastiff Fang
materials.desc: A blunt, thick canine. Cheap charms against thieves.

materials.name: Reef Shark Fin
materials.desc: A stiff grey fin; dried and boiled, it makes a gelatinous coastal soup.

materials.name: Weasel Musk Gland
materials.desc: A tiny sac of sharp, musky oil. Hunters dab it on to mask their own scent from hounds.

materials.name: Saber-Toothed Tiger Meat
materials.desc: Tough, dark big-cat meat, best smoked for the trail.

materials.name: Wolf Meat
materials.desc: Stringy, strong-tasting meat — edible when there is nothing better.

monsters.name: Hawk
monsters.blurb: A keen-eyed raptor whose flight feathers and sharp eyes are staples of the fletcher and the scryer's apprentice.

harvest.note: Pluck the long primaries only; a torn vane makes them worthless for fletching.
Delicate; must be scooped whole and sunk in brine at once.

monsters.name: Hunter Shark
monsters.blurb: A blood-scenting open-water killer; its rows of teeth, oily liver and sandpaper skin are all valuable to coastal crafters.

harvest.note: Skin it against the grain or the denticles strip away.
Render the liver within a day; spoiled liver turns rank and useless.
Must be cut out before the head is gaffed or crushed.
Dry it slowly in shade or the cartilage warps and the teeth fall out.

monsters.name: Hyena
monsters.blurb: A cackling scavenger with jaws that crack bone; its jawbone is a talisman for those who fight in packs, its hide little more than a rank tent-flap.

monsters.name: Jackal
monsters.blurb: A skulking desert dog whose sharp nose and ears make its parts useful to scouts and trackers.

harvest.note: Dry them in shade; direct sun cracks the cartilage.

monsters.name: Killer Whale
monsters.blurb: A cunning, echo-seeing sea hunter; its blubber, teeth and the oily melon of its skull are treasures of polar coasts.

harvest.note: Slice carefully around it; a nicked melon leaks and loses its focus.
Must be tied off before the carcass sinks or the air is lost.

monsters.name: Lion
monsters.blurb: The pride-leader of the plains; its mane and heart are symbols of courage in every culture that knows it.

harvest.note: Only males bear a full mane; take it with the scalp to keep it intact.

monsters.name: Lizard
monsters.blurb: A common basking lizard; its shed tail is an old hedge-witch ingredient.

harvest.note: Grab the lizard too hard and it drops the tail and escapes — which is fine.

monsters.name: Mammoth
monsters.blurb: A shaggy, tusked giant of the frozen steppe; its ivory, wool and fat keep whole tribes alive through winter.

harvest.note: Each tusk needs hours of sawing; hurry and it splits along the growth rings.

monsters.name: Mastiff
monsters.blurb: A loyal guard dog with an unerring nose; its teeth and hide are humble but honest goods.

harvest.note: Many folk consider butchering a war-dog shameful; expect hard looks in town.

monsters.name: Mule
monsters.blurb: A stubborn, sure-footed pack animal whose sinews and hooves are prized for hauling gear.

harvest.note: Tail and mane hair, cut without harm to a living animal too.

monsters.name: Octopus
monsters.blurb: A clever tidepool hunter that changes colour and vanishes in a cloud of ink.

harvest.note: Squeeze the body carelessly and it jets its ink away in death.

monsters.name: Owl
monsters.blurb: A silent night hunter; its feathers muffle sound and its eyes drink the dark.

harvest.note: Harvest at night; alchemists claim sunlight dulls them.

monsters.name: Panther
monsters.blurb: A black-coated ambusher of the forest canopy; its pelt is the quiet hunter's cloak of choice.

harvest.note: Nicks show as pale scars in the fur; skin it slowly.

monsters.name: Plesiosaurus
monsters.blurb: A long-necked marine reptile that dives deep and long; its lungs and flippers are sought for water-work.

harvest.note: Deflates and rots quickly out of water; pack it in wet kelp.

monsters.name: Poisonous Snake
monsters.blurb: A small, brightly banded viper; its venom sac is the cheapest reliable poison a rogue can find.

harvest.note: Fail by 5 or more and you nick yourself on a fang: take the snake's poison as if bitten.

monsters.name: Polar Bear
monsters.blurb: The white ice-hunter, huge and patient; its fat and pelt keep hunters alive where nothing else could.

harvest.note: Keep it out of blood; stains never quite wash out of the white.
Wise hunters bury it; hungry ones get very ill.

monsters.name: Pony
monsters.blurb: A small, hardy mount; its hair and hide are everyday goods.

harvest.note: Shared by all horse-kin.
Tail and mane hair, cut without harm to a living animal too.

monsters.name: Quipper
monsters.blurb: A little river fish with a terrible bite; alone it's a snack, its teeth are what count.

harvest.note: Fingers near the jaw can still get bitten in the death twitch.

monsters.name: Rat
monsters.blurb: Ubiquitous vermin; worthless alone, but its parts have a place in hedge-craft.

harvest.note: Wear gloves; a scratch can pass on filth fever.

monsters.name: Raven
monsters.blurb: A clever black bird that mimics voices; its feathers are the traditional quill of scholars and spies.

harvest.note: The bird's mimicry is said to fade if the tongue is taken after dawn.
Take them quickly; other ravens go for the eyes of the fallen first.

monsters.name: Reef Shark
monsters.blurb: A pack-hunting shark of warm shallows; smaller cousin of the hunter shark with similarly useful parts.

monsters.name: Rhinoceros
monsters.blurb: An armoured, short-sighted charger; its horn and hide are both famously hard.

harvest.note: Saw it at the base; hacking splinters the fibres.

monsters.name: Riding Horse
monsters.blurb: The common saddle horse; its parts are workaday goods, but its sinews carry some of its speed.

harvest.note: Tail and mane hair, cut without harm to a living animal too.

monsters.name: Warhorse
monsters.blurb: A heavy, battle-trained charger; its heart and hooves carry the reputation of steadfast courage.

harvest.note: Tail and mane hair, cut without harm to a living animal too.

monsters.name: Saber-Toothed Tiger
monsters.blurb: An ice-age cat with dagger-length fangs; its sabres are among the finest natural blades.

harvest.note: Must be extracted with the root; cracked sabres are worth a third.

monsters.name: Scorpion
monsters.blurb: A small, venomous desert arachnid; its stinger is the prize, its shell a curiosity.

harvest.note: Fail by 5 or more and the barb pierces your glove: you are poisoned as by its sting.

monsters.name: Sea Horse
monsters.blurb: A delicate, drifting fish; dried whole it's an old sailor's charm for safe waters.

harvest.note: Dry it in the sun on a flat stone or it curls unevenly and crumbles.

monsters.name: Spider
monsters.blurb: A common web-spinner; its silk and venom are small but steady trade goods.

harvest.note: Spool it from the web and spinnerets together, or it tangles into uselessness.
Fail by 5 or more and it bites you on the way: you suffer its poison.

monsters.name: Tiger
monsters.blurb: A striped, solitary jungle hunter, swift and silent; its pelt and whiskers are sought by the stealthy.

harvest.note: Arrow and spear holes ruin its value; best taken from a clean kill.

monsters.name: Triceratops
monsters.blurb: A three-horned herbivore with a bony frill; its armour-grade parts are the pride of any jungle smith.

harvest.note: The frill cracks if you pry it before the skin is fully peeled back.

monsters.name: Tyrannosaurus Rex
monsters.blurb: The tyrant lizard, apex of the jungle; its teeth, roar and heart are the stuff of legend among hunters.

harvest.note: Needs two harvesters and a saw through the ribcage; a pierced chamber floods it with blood and ruins it.

monsters.name: Vulture
monsters.blurb: A bald carrion bird with an iron gut; its stomach and feathers are tied to disease and death lore.

harvest.note: Handle with gloves; the juices burn skin.

monsters.name: Weasel
monsters.blurb: A slinky, sharp-nosed predator; its pelt is a small, sleek fur for trim and charms.

harvest.note: Burst it and you'll reek for a day; hounds and sentries will notice.

monsters.name: Wolf
monsters.blurb: The grey pack hunter; its pelt, fangs and nose are the classic trophies of the ranger.

harvest.note: Winter pelts fetch double; summer ones are thin and mangy.

monsters.name: Swarm of Bats
monsters.blurb: A shrieking cloud of bats; afterwards the cave floor is littered with wings and guano.

harvest.note: Collect only the unbroken ones.
Wear a cloth over your face; guano dust breeds cave sickness.

monsters.name: Swarm of Beetles
monsters.blurb: A clattering carpet of beetles; the fallen yield glittering shell chips and pungent grubs.

monsters.name: Swarm of Centipedes
monsters.blurb: A writhing mass of centipedes whose paralytic bites leave a harvest of tiny venom claws.

harvest.note: Fail by 5 or more and a still-twitching centipede bites you: you are exposed to its poison.

monsters.name: Swarm of Insects
monsters.blurb: A buzzing cloud of biting insects; the dead leave chitin dust and wings for hedge alchemy.

monsters.name: Swarm of Poisonous Snakes
monsters.blurb: A seething knot of vipers; dangerous to harvest, but it yields a rich haul of venom.

harvest.note: Every harvest roll that fails by 5 or more means a surviving snake bites: take its poison.

monsters.name: Swarm of Quippers
monsters.blurb: A frenzied school of flesh-stripping fish; the teeth of the dead are a crafter's windfall.

harvest.note: Harvest from shore; any blood in the water draws the rest back.

monsters.name: Swarm of Rats
monsters.blurb: A squealing tide of rats from the sewers; the haul is filthy but plentiful.

harvest.note: Gloves or a DC 10 Con save against filth fever.

monsters.name: Swarm of Ravens
monsters.blurb: A storm of black wings and beaks; the fallen birds shed a scribe's fortune in quills.

harvest.note: Pecked-out eyes are common in a swarm; only a few come intact.

monsters.name: Swarm of Spiders
monsters.blurb: A skittering carpet of spiders; their webs and venom sacs can be gathered by the careful.

harvest.note: Fail by 5 or more and a survivor bites: you suffer its poison.

monsters.name: Swarm of Wasps
monsters.blurb: An angry cloud of wasps, and usually a paper nest nearby worth the risk.

harvest.note: Fail by 5 or more and you're stung repeatedly: take the swarm's poison.
Smoke the nest first unless you want another fight.
